lead.headline: FEMA, the disaster agency, took a median 110 days to publish Jan-Jun 2025 disaster declarations, versus 41-48 days before
lead.number: Median 110 days from declaration to FEMA's first Federal Register notice for Jan-Jun 2025 disasters vs 41-48 in 2023-24; California's January 2025 fires waited 223 days; FEMA printed declaration notices on 3 days in Jan 2025-Aug 2026, while SBA printed the same disasters in 1-3 weeks
lead.watch_out: FEMA's batch "omnibus" notices carry no DR number in the docket, so a DR-number join misses them; check the notice text before calling anything a first notice

sources.quote: approvals are taking more than a month, on average.
sources.page_context: e AP’s analysis found that, on average, it took less than two weeks for a major disaster declaration to be granted by presidents throughout the 1990s and early 2000s. During the last decade, under presidents from both political parties, that rose to about three weeks. In Trump’s second term so far, approvals are taking more than a month, on average.
